title: Optimize recommendations UI sketchbook — batching, caching, quantization
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc for the Optimize tab recommendations UI — specifically the surface that suggests batching, prefix/KV caching and quantization settings for a given route/model workload. This is intentionally rough: sketches, interaction notes, acceptance criteria and a prioritized backlog for grooming.

High-level goals:
- Make recommendations actionable: 1-click apply (or preview + apply) for safe ops flows.
- Tie recommendations to metrics: estimated cost delta, expected latency impact, and confidence score.
- Avoid surprises: show constraints (hardware compatibility, model fidelity risk, cached-entry hit-rate assumptions).
- Surface progressive disclosure: show simple suggestions first, allow advanced tuning for power users.

Primary persona(s):
- Platform engineer (wants safe throughput/latency wins, can roll back).
- ML infra engineer (evaluates quantization/tradeoffs).
- Product engineer (wants quick cost savings without regressions).

Context / inputs used by recommendations engine (assume available from backend):
- Recent request distribution (seq lengths, tokens per request)
- Per-route latency p50/p95 and token breakdowns
- Model variant(s) available and quantization compatibility list
- Cache hit rates for longest common prefixes and KV cache usefulness
- Hardware profile (A100/V100/GPU memory/capacity) and whether mixing CPU fallback allowed

Notes + quick wireframe sketches (ASCII + microcopy):
[Top-level card] Route: /generate-summary  (model: redwood-v2-medium, gpu-pool: r-dedicated-eu)
- Cost per 1k tokens: $0.12  •  p50 latency: 210ms  •  p95 latency: 450ms

[Recommendation strip] (left) Badge: "High confidence"  •  (center) Short text: "Enable request batching (5–10s window) — estimated -25% cost, +30ms p50"  •  (right) CTA: [Preview] [Apply]
Microcopy under strip: "Estimates based on last 7d traffic and simulating continuous batching with your current autoscale profile."

Sketch: expanded preview modal:
- Title: Simulate batching for /generate-summary
- Inputs: target batch size (auto-suggested 16), max latency allowance (ms), fallback policy (serve-unbatched after X ms)
- Visual: small chart showing token throughput vs latency (before/after)
- Bottom: risk checklist: "may increase p95 for < 1% of requests", "compatible with current endpoint timeout 10s"
- CTA row: [Apply to Route] [Save as Rule] [Cancel]

Caching recommendation sketch:
- Card header: "Prefix/KV caching — medium confidence"
- Blurb: "Common prefixes already present for 42% of requests. Enabling prefix cache expected to reduce tokens-per-request by ~18% and reduce cost by ~12%."
- Controls: TTL suggestion (30m), scope: route-only / service-wide, preview sample (shows 3 example requests that would hit cache)
- Danger text: "Verify that responses are safe to share across similar requests (no user-specific tokens)"

Quantization suggestion sketch:
- Card: "Suggest 4-bit quantized variant of redwood-v2-medium"
- Metrics shown: estimated throughput improvement (x2), estimated token cost delta (-40%), estimated quality delta (perplexity change / small risk flag)
- Compatibility matrix: lists hardware supported, whether KV cache works with quantized kernel, and whether LLAMA-attention style optimizations are needed
- CTA: [Try on Canary (5% traffic)] [Request Dedicated Profile (ops)]

Progressive disclosure and UX states:
- Compact state: single-line recommendation with delta numbers and confidence badge, quick CTA.
- Expanded state: editing controls, simulations (charts + estimated numbers), linked logs/sample requests, and safety checkboxes (policy guardrails).
- Applied state: shows history entry (who applied, when), quick revert (rollout window + canary controls).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
1) For each route, show up to 3 top recommendations (batching, caching, quant) with: predicted cost delta, latency impact, and confidence.
2) Each recommendation must have a Preview modal that simulates impact using last 7d telemetry.
3) From Preview, user can Apply to route or Save as Rule. Apply should create a change request tracked in Console change history.
4) Safety warnings must be shown for caching and quantization with required checkbox acknowledge for caching when potential data-safety risk detected.
5) All UI elements must be keyboard accessible and pass basic a11y contrast checks.

Backlog (prioritized, groom-ready):
- OPT-101: Data contract for recommendations API (fields: delta_cost_pct, delta_latency_ms_p50, confidence, risk_flags, sample_requests) — owner: eng-applied-ml
- OPT-102: Compact recommendation list component (design + react) — owner: console-and-tooling
- OPT-103: Preview simulator backend job (runs quick sim over last-N days) — owner: serving-runtime
- OPT-104: Apply flow & audit log entry (requires RBAC, rollback) — owner: platform-engineering
- OPT-105: Quantization compatibility matrix service (hardware × model table) — owner: infrastructure
- OPT-106: Sample request recycler for cache preview (sanitizer + examples) — owner: product-optimize
- OPT-107: Canary rollout UI extension for Apply flow (traffic % slider, metrics watch) — owner: release-engineering

Grooming notes (from meeting 2026-03-09):
- Team agreed MVP should not auto-apply anything — always require user confirmation.
- For preview sims, we should expose the underlying assumptions in a collapsible area (e.g., "Assumptions: tokenization uniform, hit rate extrapolated from last 7d").
- For quantization, show an A/B sample text generation comparison (side-by-side) for a handful of canonical prompts — if quality delta is high, mark "manual review required".

Open questions / risks:
- Data-safety: how do we accurately detect user-specific tokens to avoid caching PII? (Need input from security/compliance).
- Estimation fidelity: sim could mispredict when traffic pattern changes (weekday vs weekend). We need a confidence calibration workstream.
- Rollback complexity: if caching is applied and a downstream service depends on request idempotency, revert may not be instantaneous. Need ops runbook.

Micro-interactions & copy drafts:
- Badge text for low/medium/high confidence with color tokens: "Low (🔴)", "Medium (🟡)", "High (🟢)" (replace emoji with icons)
- Batching CTA: "Preview simulated batching" / Apply = "Enable batching (will create change request)"
- Caching safety modal headline: "Cache may expose shared responses — review before enabling"

Telemetry / metrics to show post-apply (for rollout page):
- actual cost delta vs estimated (% tokens, $)
- p50/p95 latency change over time
- cache hit rate over time (prefix vs KV)
- error spike indicator (5xx / time)

Next steps (short-term):
- Make OPT-101 and OPT-102 groom-ready by 2026-03-17. Liam to own data contract doc, Ava to iterate on compact-list component wireframes.
- Sync with security on caching PII detection by 2026-03-20.
- Create a small usability test: 5 platform engineers run the Preview flow and give feedback on trust/confidence. Draft script by 2026-03-18.

Misc rough notes (freeform):
- Could we allow "simulate with synthetic traffic" toggle? Helpful for low-traffic endpoints.
- Consider a feature flag to enable aggressive batching suggestions for dedicated customers only.
- Maybe use a "confidence thermometer" that combines model of traffic volatility, sample size and historical sim accuracy.

End of sketchbook.

Revision history (high level):
- 2025-11-04: initial notes, early sketches
- 2026-01-12: added quantization card ideas and compatibility table notes
- 2026-03-09: grooming meeting notes and backlog list added
- 2026-03-10: updated acceptance criteria and next steps
